findings.description: The copied `GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn` declares `availability.days` as `string[]`, but Prisma's list response and `getScheduleListItemData` require `number[]`. `ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper` passes each returned schedule to that transformer and the whole list to `useEnsureDefaultSchedule` (also typed with numeric days), so TypeScript rejects the atoms package on these mainline calls. Declare the days as `number[]`.
findings.failureMode: TS compile failure in schedule list transformer and default-schedule hook
findings.title: Use numeric availability days in the local schedule response

findings.description: The new slot response declares `fromUser.id` as a string, but the returned slots use `IFromUser` with numeric IDs. `EventTypeCalendarViewComponent` passes `schedule.data` to `useAvailableTimeSlots`, which still accepts `IGetAvailableSlots` with numeric `fromUser.id`; TypeScript now rejects that call and the atoms type-check fails. Make this ID a number to match the server contract.
findings.failureMode: TypeScript incompatibility when passing available slots to calendar view
findings.title: Keep numeric IDs in available-slot `fromUser`

findings.description: The expanded `@calcom/trpc/**` block now matches `QueryCell` imports already present in the conferencing-apps and selected-calendars atoms wrappers; running lint on the package will fail even though those imports are not removed by this change.
findings.failureMode: Biome noRestrictedImports errors in atoms package lint
findings.title: New restriction breaks lint on existing atoms imports

findings.description: This new file uses single-quoted JS strings at lines 39, 40, 45 and 46 despite the configured double-quote format; `biome format packages/platform/atoms/hooks/schedules/types.ts` exits with an error instead of passing. Format these strings with Biome.
findings.failureMode: Biome formatter check exits nonzero on the new schedule types file
findings.title: Format new schedule validation file with Biome

findings.description: API v2 builds with `nest build` to CommonJS and previously accesses TeamService via `@calcom/platform-libraries`; this new direct deep import resolves to `packages/features/.../teamService.ts`, which has no built JS distribution for Node's production `start:prod`. Loading the new controller on app startup therefore fails with a module-resolution error. Use the existing compiled platform-libraries TeamService export.
findings.failureMode: Production API startup fails when Nest requires an uncompiled TS deep import from @calcom/features.
findings.title: Import the compiled platform library rather than features source

findings.description: A TEAM_MEMBER passes RolesGuard's minimum-role comparison and can call TeamService.createInvite, generating a redeemable invitation despite the admin-only contract. Set the role to TEAM_ADMIN.
findings.failureMode: Any ordinary team member can generate invite tokens without admin authority.
findings.title: Require team admin to create invites

findings.description: A caller who is an admin of a sub-team under an organization with Admin API access disabled is rejected on the existing `/v2/organizations/:orgId/teams/:teamId/invite` route by IsAdminAPIEnabledGuard, yet the newly registered generic `/v2/teams/:teamId/invite` route has no such guard and calls the same TeamService.createInvite on that team ID, returning a usable link. Enforce the equivalent org-specific entitlement on this route when the team has a parent organization.
findings.failureMode: Org team admin can bypass disabled organization Admin API by using generic team invite endpoint.
findings.title: Preserve org Admin API gating on org team invites

findings.description: For a newly created invite, `identifier` is the fixed `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` while the persisted random `token` is used in inviteLink and token lookup. The API returns an unusable token to clients, and repeated calls return the same reported token; return `newToken.token` instead.
findings.failureMode: Creating an invite returns a token that cannot be redeemed and disagrees with inviteLink.
findings.title: Return the generated invite token, not its identifier

findings.description: `isOrgContext` is true for an org or sub-team; changing the branch from `!isOrgContext` sends their invites to `/teams` instead of `/signup?...&callbackUrl=...`, skipping the invitation signup/onboarding path for new org users. It also sends ordinary team invites to `/signup` instead of the `/teams?token=` page that consumes them. Restore the base condition so the link matches each context.
findings.failureMode: Organization new invitee receives login/team page instead of signup; existing regular-team invitee is sent to signup instead of team token handler.
findings.title: Do not invert invite link routing for regular and organization teams

findings.description: An authenticated team MEMBER satisfies RolesGuard's minimum-role check for `TEAM_MEMBER`, so POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite creates a shareable invite without admin rights; the non-admin 403 test instead receives 200. Require `TEAM_ADMIN`.
findings.failureMode: Authenticated MEMBER in team POSTs /v2/teams/{id}/invite; unauthorized invitation token is created and response is 200.
findings.title: Require team admin role for invite creation

findings.description: An org subteam administrator can post `/v2/teams/:teamId/invite` even if its organization's Admin API access is disabled, whereas the existing org-team invite route includes `IsAdminAPIEnabledGuard` and rejects that same operation. Gate org subteam invites equivalently (resolve parent org first).
findings.failureMode: Org with Admin API access disabled, authenticated subteam admin sends invite to /v2/teams/{subteamId}/invite and succeeds instead of 403 from org-team invite endpoint.
findings.title: Do not bypass org Admin API gate via team invite URL

findings.description: For every new invite the response sends `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` rather than the 64-character stored token. The inviteLink uses the actual token, so consumers who share/use the returned token cannot join; repeated requests return the same apparent token and E2E uniqueness/link assertions fail. Return `newToken.token` instead.
findings.failureMode: Create invite for any team; response token differs from persisted verification token and link query.
findings.title: Return actual invite token instead of identifier

findings.description: For an organization or its subteam the new condition returns `/teams?token=...` rather than the signup link, while a regular team is sent to `/signup` rather than `/teams`. Invite recipients are routed through the wrong flow. Restore the old branch condition.
findings.failureMode: Creating invitation for org or ordinary team now produces opposite signup destination from base.
findings.title: Preserve organization-aware invite link routing

findings.description: The `@calcom/features/...` import violates the API v2 Biome `noRestrictedImports` rule; running Biome lint reports an error on line 21 and fails the check. Import `TeamService` via `@calcom/platform-libraries`, as the existing organizations invite controller does.
findings.failureMode: Run Biome lint against new API v2 controller; noRestrictedImports error blocks lint.
findings.title: Use the permitted platform service import in API v2

findings.description: `GetUser` is never referenced in the new controller. Biome flags it with `noUnusedImports` warning, and the staged-file lint command uses `--error-on-warnings`, so this file fails that check even after fixing the forbidden TeamService import. Remove the unused import.
findings.failureMode: Run Biome lint --error-on-warnings on the new controller after fixing the restricted import; lint still fails due to unused GetUser.
findings.title: Remove unused GetUser import that fails strict lint

findings.description: Biome format rejects this manually split import block under the required 110-character configuration. Running the formatter/check on the new controller fails; use the Biome-produced single-line import.
findings.failureMode: biome format on changed controller exits nonzero for changed Nest import block.
findings.title: Format Nest controller imports with Biome

findings.description: Biome format rejects the split createInvite signature; the required formatting check exits nonzero. Write the signature on one line as Biome prescribes.
findings.failureMode: biome format on changed controller exits nonzero for method declaration.
findings.title: Format invite handler signature with Biome

findings.description: The changed file ends without a newline; Biome format fails on this changed file. Restore the final newline so the formatter check passes.
findings.failureMode: biome format on teamService exits nonzero for missing final newline.
findings.title: Keep final newline in teamService

findings.description: Both macOS jobs now use macOS-15 but still run `xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer` (lines 166 and 392). The macOS-15 image ships Xcode 16.4, not the 15.2 path, so that setup step fails before any build or tests. Update both path values to a version actually present on macOS-15.
findings.failureMode: macOS-15 build jobs fail at xcode-select on nonexistent Xcode_15.2.0.app.
findings.title: Select an Xcode installed on macOS-15

findings.description: For a 10.0.2 servicing build with a baseline package reference removed, the new `AspNetCorePatchVersion == 1` gate skips BUILD002 entirely and allows a changed dependency graph to ship; the previous condition checked every servicing patch. Remove that patch-number restriction so removed references still fail restore.
findings.failureMode: 10.0.2 servicing build with a removed BaselinePackageReference no longer raises BUILD002.
findings.title: Do not disable baseline-reference guard after patch 1

findings.description: When this change switches to servicing 10.0.1, `PreviousAspNetCoreReleaseVersion` becomes 10.0.0 while `eng/Baseline.Designer.props` remains at 9.0.0. `ValidateBaseline=false` bypasses the check that catches this; with a servicing build setting `IsPackageInThisPatch=false` for an unchanged package, `Directory.Build.targets` instead assigns that package's `BaselinePackageVersion`/assembly version from 9.0.0 rather than the required 10.0.0. Update both baseline files from 10.0.0 and restore validation.
findings.failureMode: Unpatched project in the 10.0.1 servicing build receives 9.0.0 baseline assembly/package version, with the stale-baseline build check disabled.
findings.title: Refresh the package baseline before disabling its guard

findings.description: The changed namespace declaration switches this C# file from file-scoped to block-scoped, contrary to both the mandatory repository rule and `.editorconfig`'s `csharp_style_namespace_declarations = file_scoped`; C# namespace-format verification flags the file. Keep `namespace ...;` and remove its new closing brace.
findings.failureMode: C# file-scoped namespace format check fails on the changed test file.
findings.title: Keep the test namespace file-scoped

findings.description: `make check` runs `ruff check ./api` without auto-fixing; this new assertion triggers SIM300 (Yoda condition), causing the code check to fail. Put `result.outputs["output"]` on the left.
findings.failureMode: Ruff code-check fails at SIM300.
findings.title: Fix reversed assertion that fails Ruff check

findings.description: The added `test_run_with_boolean_values` and every other newly added run test constructs `TemplateTransformNode(..., graph=mock_graph, ...)`, but its constructor accepts no `graph` argument; these tests error with TypeError before asserting anything. Remove the unsupported argument (and supply a valid node config) at the added sites.
findings.failureMode: Running newly added template node tests fails at construction with unexpected keyword argument `graph`.
findings.title: New template tests pass an unsupported `graph` argument

findings.description: All newly added run tests pass a bare `node_data` dict as `config`; `Node.__init__` requires `config['id']` and reads template settings from `config['data']`. After removing the separate unsupported `graph` argument, these tests fail with `ValueError('Node ID is required.')` rather than exercise rendering. Wrap each test's node_data in `{'id': 'test_node', 'data': node_data}`.
findings.failureMode: New tests cannot construct node even once unsupported graph argument is removed.
findings.title: Give added tests a node-shaped config

findings.description: This added test sets the pool value to None, but `default('N/A')` does not replace defined None in Jinja2; real rendering yields `None`, while the mocked renderer returns `N/A`. Thus the test asserts incorrect output and masks missing-value behavior. Use `default('N/A', true)` in the test template for the intended fallback and exercise the real renderer.
findings.failureMode: Missing optional variable renders as 'None' in production while the new test claims 'N/A'.
findings.title: Match Jinja's default filter behavior for None

findings.description: `ruff format --check` reports the changed file would be reformatted because this test definition is split across lines; format it on one line.
findings.failureMode: Formatting check fails on the changed test file.
findings.title: Format concatenation test to pass Ruff format check

findings.description: `ruff format --check` reports the changed file would be reformatted because this second function definition is split across lines; format it on one line.
findings.failureMode: Formatting check fails on the changed test file.
findings.title: Format conditional test to pass Ruff format check

findings.description: After `HSETEX h EX 100 FIELDS 1 f 1`, `HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1.1` now calls `hashTypeSet` without `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL`, which strips the primary's TTL (`HTTL` becomes -1). The rewritten `HSETEX ... KEEPTTL` retains the TTL on a replica, so the primary and replica diverge and the field no longer expires on the primary. Keep `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` in this local write.
findings.failureMode: For a live field with TTL, HINCRBYFLOAT persists it on primary and leaves it expiring on replica.
findings.title: Preserve the field TTL on the primary increment

findings.description: With swiping tabs enabled, the toolbar leading edge now equals the right skeleton's trailing edge, while its trailing edge still equals that same skeleton's leading edge. Because the right skeleton has positive width, this imposes a negative width on the main toolbar and pushes it offscreen / triggers Auto Layout constraint breaks. Restore leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor on the leading constraint.
findings.failureMode: Main address toolbar collapses or moves offscreen when tab swiping enabled
findings.title: Anchor the center toolbar to the left skeleton bar

findings.description: With a newly inserted trailing page action (e.g. reload/stop), updateActionStack sets its alpha to 0, but updateToolbarLayout lists browserActionStack twice rather than trailingPageActionStack. No animation or nonanimated layout restores the trailing action alpha, so the button stays invisible. Use trailingPageActionStack in the fourth term.
findings.failureMode: New trailing page-action buttons remain invisible
findings.title: Restore trailing page actions to the fade-in set

findings.description: For BrowserAddressToolbar configured with `.default()` UX (4-pt divider) and a trailing reload/stop action but no leading action, this new test sets the divider to zero, shrinking the spacing before the trailing button; with only a leading action it adds a spurious gap. The divider is adjacent to trailingPageActionStack (and the old code checked it); check that stack instead. Firefox currently passes `.experiment()` with a zero divider, but `.default()` is a public, usable configuration.
findings.failureMode: Wrong address text/button spacing with default UX and mismatched leading/trailing actions
findings.title: Keep divider spacing tied to trailing page actions

findings.description: `prepare_tools` returns `crate::Result<PathBuf>`, but its `?` calls to the changed `write_and_make_executable` return `FileWriteError` and there is no `From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error`. Linux builds fail with E0277; return `std::io::Result` again or add a matching conversion.
findings.failureMode: Linux cargo check fails to compile E0277
findings.title: Convert FileWriteError into the bundler error

findings.description: On a fresh cache the path does not exist, so `set_permissions(path, ...)` returns NotFound before `fs::write` can create it. AppImage bundling fails on the first AppRun download (and any new plugin); write the file first, then set its permissions.
findings.failureMode: fresh AppImage bundle fails with ENOENT in prepare_tools
findings.title: Write downloaded tools before setting permissions

findings.description: When the cache has no `linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh`, this inverted condition skips creating it, although `bundle_project` always invokes linuxdeploy with `--plugin gtk`. After the other tool-write issues are fixed, a fresh AppImage bundle still fails because linuxdeploy cannot find the GTK plugin. Change the guard to `!gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: fresh AppImage bundle lacks mandatory GTK plugin
findings.title: Create the GTK plugin on a fresh tools cache

findings.description: The new macOS-15 image does not contain /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app, but both job branches still run sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer (lines 166 and 392). Their selection step fails before any build. Update the selection path to Xcode_16.4.0.app in both branches along with the pool migration.
findings.failureMode: Hosted or official macOS-15 job fails at xcode-select because Xcode 15.2 is absent.
findings.title: Switch the Xcode select step with the macOS-15 pool

findings.description: AspNetCorePatchVersion=1 implies a 10.0.0 baseline, but Baseline.Designer.props is still 9.0.0. Setting ValidateBaseline=false bypasses the only version check; for a servicing build excluding an unchanged package (`IsPackageInThisPatch=false`), Directory.Build.targets uses its 9.0.0 BaselinePackageVersion as the assembly and package dependency version, rather than the released 10.0.0 version. Regenerate the 10.0.0 baseline and restore validation.
findings.failureMode: An excluded 10.0.1 servicing package resolves/brands as 9.0.0 rather than retaining its 10.0.0 release baseline.
findings.title: Do not disable the stale servicing baseline check

findings.description: With AspNetCorePatchVersion=2 and a baseline dependency removed from a shipping project, BUILD002 no longer runs, so a servicing package can silently drop a dependency. Remove the patch-version equality and preserve the servicing check.
findings.failureMode: Servicing patch 10.0.2 accidentally removes a baseline package reference and builds without BUILD002; downstream consumers may lose a dependency.
findings.title: Keep removed-reference check enabled for later servicing patches

findings.description: The test file switches from a file-scoped namespace to a block-scoped namespace, contrary to the repository's mandatory namespace rule; source-format compliance checks will reject the changed file. Restore the semicolon namespace and remove the wrapping braces.
findings.failureMode: The modified C# test file violates the mandatory file-scoped namespace rule, failing namespace compliance validation.
findings.title: Retain file-scoped namespace in WebSocket compression tests

findings.description: `showReaderMode` now sets `.readerModeLongPressAction`, which BVC handles by calling `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()` instead of `toggleReaderMode()`. On a normal tap of the reader icon the page is inserted into the profile's persistent reading list and reader mode does not toggle; this also persists private-tab URLs without the user opting to save them. Restore `.readerMode` for the tap action.
findings.failureMode: reader-mode tap persists private page to reading list and does not toggle reader mode
findings.title: Reader-mode tap saves pages to Reading List instead of opening reader mode

findings.description: On a reader-mode tab, selecting Menu or Tabs calls `cancelEditMode`. Reader URLs are `http://localhost/reader-mode/page?...` and satisfy `isWebPage()`, so this changed `||` dispatches the internal URL; the cancel-edit reducer assigns it to the address-bar URL and LocationView prints its absolute string, replacing the decoded real site URL. Keep excluding `isReaderModeURL` here as before.
findings.failureMode: cancel edit while on reader page replaces real site URL with internal localhost URL
findings.title: Canceling edit exposes localhost reader URL in address bar

findings.description: For the default/active reader state, the new `default: true` is passed as `isEnabled` into `readerModeButtonTapped`, whose existing `ReaderModeButtonTappedExtra` initializer assigns it to `isPrivate`. A reader-mode tap in a normal tab therefore reports `isPrivate=true` (and `testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes` now fails its `isPrivate == false` assertion with the default nil state). Restore the prior `available: true`/`default: false` mapping; the swapped extras in `ToolbarTelemetry` predate this PR.
findings.failureMode: reader-mode event on normal active/default state misreports private mode and existing unit test fails
findings.title: Inverted reader-state mapping breaks privacy telemetry and existing test

findings.description: With ClickZetta's configured `quote` string-literal mode, this Python string emits `ESCAPE '\\'` with two backslashes inside the SQL literal, although LIKE ESCAPE must be a single character. If full-text retrieval fails and calls `_search_by_like`, the query is rejected instead of retrieving documents. Emit a single escape character for the active quote mode (or use a different one-character delimiter).
findings.failureMode: ClickZetta fallback retrieval fails SQL execution for all searches
findings.title: Use a one-character ClickZetta ESCAPE literal

findings.description: WorkflowRun.inputs/outputs are persisted with default `json.dumps`, so Chinese text such as `你好` is stored as `\u4f60\u597d`, not as literal characters. Replacing the prior `unicode_escape` conversion with `escape_like_pattern(keyword[:30])` searches for literal `你好` and returns zero workflow app logs for a run containing it. Convert the keyword to the JSON representation before escaping the LIKE metacharacters.
findings.failureMode: non-ASCII workflow-run keyword searches return no matching logs
findings.title: Preserve Unicode-escaped matching of workflow JSON

findings.description: With IRIS_TEXT_INDEX disabled, the helper turns `%` into `\%`, but `ESCAPE '|'` makes backslash literal and leaves `%` as a wildcard. Querying for `50%` fails to find text containing `50%` and can match `50\abc` instead; escape using `|` or set the SQL escape to backslash.
findings.failureMode: IRIS full-text fallback returns wrong documents for literal percent/underscore/backslash searches
findings.title: Use the same LIKE escape character in IRIS as the helper

findings.description: Unlike the three adjacent LIKE branches, `not contains` applies the helper's backslash escapes without passing `escape='\\'` to SQL. On a backend with no implicit backslash LIKE escape (e.g. SQLite tests or MySQL configured with `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES`), searching for `not contains '50%'` includes a document whose metadata is `50% discount` (and may exclude `50\\abc` instead). Add the explicit escape clause to the negated filter.
findings.failureMode: not contains metadata returns documents that contain the excluded substring
findings.title: Supply the escape clause for the negated contains filter

findings.description: When a compact onboarding card's `forward*` button is tapped, `OnboardingViewCompact.handleBottomButtonAction` posts `.screenChanged` immediately after the view-model callback. The new `Task` defers `handleAction` and its `.advance` completion until after that post, so `pageCount` still selects the old card when the accessibility event is emitted; VoiceOver can refocus/announce the old card, and `.onChange` does not post a replacement. Keep synchronous forward handling on the main actor or move the accessibility notification after advancing.
findings.failureMode: Compact onboarding forward taps announce/refocus the previous card with VoiceOver instead of the destination card.
findings.title: Post the forward accessibility event after the page advances

findings.description: After `HSETEX h EX 100 FIELDS 1 f 1`, `HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1.1` now strips the primary field expiry (`HTTL` returns `-1`), because this local `hashTypeSet` dropped `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL`. The rewritten HSETEX KEEPTTL only affects propagation, not the already-executed primary write, so replicas/AOF can retain the expiry the primary has lost. Restore `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` here; the existing TTL-preservation test also fails without it.
findings.failureMode: The primary retains a value permanently instead of expiring it, and disagrees with a replica or AOF replay that kept the TTL.
findings.title: Keep TTL on the primary HINCRBYFLOAT write

findings.description: `addHashFieldToReply` is used only inside `t_hash.c`, but removing `static` gives it external linkage in non-LTO builds, violating the repository's mandatory private-helper rule. A test/object file that defines the same generic helper name can now cause a duplicate-symbol link failure; keep it `static`.
findings.failureMode: A non-LTO build that links another unit exporting addHashFieldToReply fails with a duplicate-definition linker error.
findings.title: Restore static linkage on the hash reply helper

findings.description: With a working selector, SelectLightTheme taps `lightThemeView` and the `darkThemeView` accessibility value remains `"0"`. This new lookup therefore makes `testCheckSystemThemeChanges` fail at its first assertion instead of verifying the light mode; use `lightThemeView` as before.
findings.failureMode: An otherwise-correct light theme selection fails the UI test with 0 != 1.
findings.title: Check the light button after selecting Light

findings.description: The Shortcuts row pushes `TopSitesSettingsViewController`, which has no Done button; only its parent Homepage settings controller installs one. The reordered `Done` tap now happens while still on the Shortcuts subpage, so the test times out waiting for a button that isn't there before checking the section. Pop the subpage before tapping Done.
findings.failureMode: testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection waits for a nonexistent Done button on the Shortcuts subpage.
findings.title: Back out of Shortcuts before tapping Done

findings.description: Changing strict to false also disables strictNullChecks, which TanStack Router requires. Running `tsc -b --noEmit` now exits 2 with hundreds of errors such as `Argument ... is not assignable to parameter of type '"strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json"'`; the UI build (`tsc -b && vite build`) and validate:types cannot pass. Restore strict: true rather than weakening the project check.
findings.failureMode: Running UI type validation/build with changed tsconfig causes TanStack Router type errors and halts.
findings.title: Keep strict null checks enabled for TanStack Router

findings.description: The 'Stays in' posture still writes the chosen pool status to `trigger.expect`, whereas `after` is the event that starts monitoring a state. With Proactive and Not Ready selected, the resulting trigger looks for the absence of subsequent Not Ready events (and can fire when the pool has become Ready), instead of timing how long it stays Not Ready. Select `trigger.after` for Proactive, as the flow-run and deployment status fields do.
findings.failureMode: Select Stays in Not Ready for a work pool; a saved proactive automation checks for missing Not Ready events instead of the pool staying Not Ready.
findings.title: Use after for proactive work-pool status

findings.description: When the queue-status posture is 'Stays in', this field still writes the selected status to `trigger.expect`. That configures the proactive trigger to detect an absence of subsequent status events rather than a queue remaining in that status, so a queue that becomes Ready after Not Ready can cause an erroneous firing. Use `trigger.after` for Proactive as the existing flow-run and new deployment selectors do.
findings.failureMode: Choose Stays in Not Ready for a work queue; resulting trigger counts missing Not Ready events instead of measuring the duration spent Not Ready.
findings.title: Use after for proactive work-queue status

findings.description: Clearing the custom textarea produces `['']` because `''.split('\n')` has length one. The wizard schema accepts it, but the server's `expects` matches no real event name for `''`, so the saved Reactive trigger will not fire; an empty list would mean 'any event'. Filter blank lines and submit [] when cleared.
findings.failureMode: After deleting all custom event text, wizard stores expect=[''] and the resulting event trigger never fires.
findings.title: Treat a cleared custom event textarea as an empty array

findings.description: The number input accepts exponent notation such as `1e2`, but `parseInt('1e2')` stores threshold 1 instead of 100; the Zod schema accepts this wrong value. Use `Number(e.target.value)` as in the other threshold components (which also avoids the Biome lint warning).
findings.failureMode: Entering 1e2 in the work-pool threshold submits threshold 1, so the trigger fires after one event rather than 100.
findings.title: Preserve work-pool threshold entered in exponent notation

findings.description: With standard `tauri.conf.json` (`"identifier":"com.example.app"`, `"bundle":{}`), `bundle` is an object, so `as_str()` yields `None`; `tauri android build` and `tauri ios build` call `write_options`, which now returns `app configuration is missing an identifier` before building. Read `identifier` from the root as before.
findings.failureMode: Valid mobile build fails with missing-identifier error.
findings.title: Restore top-level identifier lookup for mobile builds

findings.description: A config path cannot have both `json` and `json5` extensions, so `&&` makes validation unreachable. E.g. a JSON config with `"identifier":"com.example.app","productName":"bad/name"` deserializes as a String yet violates the schema's `productName` regex; CLI now accepts it instead of reporting the validation error and exiting. Reinstate `||`.
findings.failureMode: Schema-invalid JSON config is silently accepted.
findings.title: Validate JSON or JSON5 instead of requiring both extensions

findings.description: The new 156-column `let schema` line exceeds the repository rustfmt `max_width = 100`; rustfmt splits this expression across lines. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` will fail for this changed source line. Format it before merging.
findings.failureMode: Mandatory Rust formatting check rejects the changed file.
findings.title: Format the validator initialization to pass rustfmt

findings.description: The new `Task` defers `handleAction` despite both callbacks already running on the main actor. If Set Default Browser (or Open iOS Firefox Settings) is tapped and Skip is processed before the queued task, `skipOnboarding()` completes the flow and the launch coordinator is removed, but the task retains `onboardingService` and subsequently calls `openSettings()` anyway, sending the user out of the browser after they skipped. Call `handleAction` inline to preserve tap ordering.
findings.failureMode: Tap Settings action then Skip before the queued main-actor task runs; system Settings opens after onboarding has been dismissed.
findings.title: Do not defer onboarding actions past dismissal

findings.description: Loading the members API now requires lib/magic-link/magic-link although the target remains MagicLink.js. On a case-sensitive host this raises MODULE_NOT_FOUND, blocking member signup/signin and potentially server startup. Keep the original MagicLink require until that file is renamed.
findings.failureMode: members API fails to load on Linux
findings.title: Restore the casing of the MagicLink require

findings.description: When email analytics initializes, this new lowercase require targets email-service/email-event-storage, but that directory still contains only EmailEventStorage.js. On case-sensitive hosts it throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND before constructing the analytics service; keep the require's original casing (or rename the target in the same change).
findings.failureMode: email analytics initialization crashes on case-sensitive filesystem
findings.title: Require the actual EmailEventStorage module

findings.description: During email analytics initialization, this new lowercase require targets email-service/email-event-processor, while the only implementation is still EmailEventProcessor.js. Even if the storage import is fixed, this separate missing module crashes initialization with MODULE_NOT_FOUND; retain the original casing or rename its target.
findings.failureMode: email analytics initialization crashes on case-sensitive filesystem
findings.title: Require the actual EmailEventProcessor module

findings.description: The edited requires on lines 1-4 and 6-10 omit semicolons where the base version had them, violating the repository's mandatory semicolon rule and failing lint when this file is checked. Terminate these statements with semicolons.
findings.failureMode: lint fails on members-api imports
findings.title: Restore semicolons on the new imports

findings.description: On every valid Tauri config `identifier` is a required top-level string, while `bundle` is an object. Looking up `bundle` then calling `as_str()` always gives None, so `write_options()`/`read_options()` used by mobile dev/build fail with "app configuration is missing an identifier" before the Android Studio/Xcode handoff. Keep looking up `identifier`.
findings.failureMode: Valid mobile app cannot build or run because original_identifier is None.
findings.title: Keep the top-level identifier for mobile build handoff

findings.description: An extension cannot equal both `json` and `json5`, so this `&&` makes the schema check unreachable. For example `tauri.conf.json` with `identifier: "com.example.app"` and `productName: "bad/name"` passes `Config` deserialization because the product-name regex only applies to JSON Schema, whereas the previous validator rejected it. Keep `||` so the schema validates both formats.
findings.failureMode: Invalid product names bypass schema rejection and reach CLI/bundling.
findings.title: Restore JSON/JSON5 schema validation

findings.description: Given an already loaded handle (`get(target, &[])`) followed by `merge_with(&[&json!({"build":{"devUrl":"http://localhost:8080"}})])`, the `merge(&mut value, ...)` result is discarded and `inner` retains its original `dev_url`, even though `merge_with` returns Ok. The removed `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value)...` must be restored along with the extension bookkeeping; the visible mobile callers pre-reload the same override, but the helper itself no longer fulfills its contract.
findings.failureMode: The merge_with operation reports success without updating its handle, and also stops rejecting invalid merged Config values.
findings.title: Do not discard the result of merge_with

findings.description: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails because rustfmt wraps the new long `serde_json::from_str(...).expect(...)` statement. Split it as rustfmt requires.
findings.failureMode: Rust formatting check fails on new line.
findings.title: Format the validator initialization

findings.description: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` also fails on the new single-line `.extensions.insert(...)` statement; rustfmt wraps this expression on three lines. Apply rustfmt here.
findings.failureMode: Rust formatting check fails on new line.
findings.title: Format the extension insert

findings.description: A normal reader-mode button tap dispatches `showReaderMode`, but this changed reducer now emits `.readerModeLongPressAction`. BrowserViewController handles that with `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()`, which creates a reading-list record instead of enabling/disabling reader mode. Restore `.readerMode` here; otherwise the tap silently adds the current article to reading list and does not toggle reader mode.
findings.failureMode: Reader-mode tap adds a reading-list entry and leaves reader mode unchanged.
findings.title: Restore reader-mode toggle for normal taps

findings.description: On an active reader-mode tab, `selectedTab.url` is an internal `http://localhost/reader-mode/page?...` URL while `ToolbarState.addressToolbar.url` was populated from `tab.url?.displayURL` (original site). The new `|| currentURL.isReaderModeURL` forwards the internal URL to `cancelEdit`; its reducer prefers the action URL over the existing display URL, so closing edit mode shows the localhost reader-mode URL in the location bar. Do not pass the internal reader URL; use the site's displayURL or let the state retain it.
findings.failureMode: Closing the address bar while in reader mode replaces the readable site URL with an internal localhost reader-mode URL.
findings.title: Keep the display URL when cancelling editing on reader pages

findings.description: For an already-active reader mode in normal browsing, the new `default: true` is passed as `isEnabled` to `ToolbarTelemetry.readerModeButtonTapped`, whose unchanged constructor currently uses it for the `is_private` extra. This changes `is_private` from false to true for that tap (and changes a private-mode activation from true to false). Restore available=true/default=false here; the separate pre-existing swapped-argument bug in ToolbarTelemetry still needs its own correction.
findings.failureMode: Reader-mode event incorrectly reports normal browsing as private on deactivation, and private browsing as normal on activation.
findings.title: Do not invert reader-mode telemetry toggle at the call site

findings.description: WorkflowRun.inputs/outputs are text persisted with `json.dumps` (default `ensure_ascii=True`), so a workflow input of `中文` is stored as `\u4e2d\u6587`. The removed `unicode_escape` conversion searched that representation; the replacement searches literal `中文` instead and returns no matching workflow logs. Encode the keyword to the stored JSON form before LIKE escaping for these fields (keeping the session-ID branch on raw text).
findings.failureMode: Searching non-ASCII workflow inputs/outputs returns no results
findings.title: Preserve Unicode JSON encoding when searching workflow inputs

findings.description: When IRIS_TEXT_INDEX is disabled and a user searches `50%`, `escape_like_pattern` produces `50\%` but the query declares `ESCAPE '|'`. IRIS treats `%` as a wildcard rather than a literal, returning unrelated documents (and `\` may become a required literal). Use a pipe-based escaping routine or use a backslash escape clause.
findings.failureMode: False positive/negative full-text fallback search for percent or underscore
findings.title: Match IRIS LIKE escape clause to the helper

findings.description: `prepare_tools` returns `crate::Result<PathBuf>`, but `write_and_make_executable` now returns `FileWriteError`; none of the five `?` callers can convert it into `crate::error::Error` (only `io::Error` has a `#[from]` variant), so the Linux bundler fails compilation with E0277. Keep the helper returning `std::io::Result<()>` as before and eliminate the unnecessary custom error wrapper.
findings.failureMode: tauri-bundler fails compilation with E0277
findings.title: Keep the write helper's error compatible with the bundler result

findings.description: On a clean tools cache, the first AppRun download calls this function on a nonexistent file. set_permissions returns NotFound before fs::write, so every fresh AppImage build fails. Restore write-before-chmod order.
findings.failureMode: fresh AppImage bundling fails with ENOENT
findings.title: Write tool before setting its permissions

findings.description: With a clean tools cache gtk.exists() is false so the GTK plugin is never written; linuxdeploy's mandatory --plugin gtk then cannot find it. Reverse the guard.
findings.failureMode: AppImage bundling fails due to missing GTK plugin
findings.title: Install GTK plugin when absent, not when present

findings.description: On a lib64 distro where gtk-query-immodules-3.0 or gdk-pixbuf-query-loaders is installed under /usr/lib64/<package>/ but not in PATH, the new search_tool checks a Debian multiarch path and /usr/lib only. The prior downloaded plugin searched /usr/lib64; now it misses the tool and may run sed against a missing cache, failing AppImage packaging. Restore the lib64 search path.
findings.failureMode: GTK plugin fails to find cache generator on lib64 systems and bundling aborts
findings.title: Search lib64 for GTK helper tools

findings.description: The previously downloaded GTK plugin copied GIRepository typelibs and exported GI_TYPELIB_PATH immediately after the schema hook; the inline script proceeds straight to the GTK case without either. AppImages requiring gi.repository fail to load bundled typelibs on machines with no matching system typelibs. Restore the typelib copy and export.
findings.failureMode: GTK introspection consumers fail to find typelib namespace
findings.title: Bundle GI typelibs and set the typelib search path

findings.description: If AppDir/usr/lib already contains a symlink or file named after an image loader or GTK module (e.g. supplied via bundle.files or already copied by linuxdeploy), `ln -s` fails under `set -e`, aborting the AppImage build. The previously fetched plugin used `ln -sf`; retain its overwrite behavior.
findings.failureMode: GTK plugin terminates when module link basename already exists
findings.title: Replace existing GTK module symlinks instead of aborting

findings.description: For a desktop configured with the dark color scheme but gtk-theme still named Adwaita, the new hook greps the theme name for 'dark' instead of the portal/GSettings color-scheme as in the prior remote plugin, so the AppImage launches with a light theme despite a dark preference. Restore color-scheme based selection.
findings.failureMode: AppImage displays light theme despite system dark scheme
findings.title: Read the desktop color scheme when choosing the GTK theme

findings.description: The new GTK script indents first-level blocks with four spaces, contrary to the root .editorconfig's indent_size = 2. Running an EditorConfig standards check flags it; reindent to two spaces per level.
findings.failureMode: EditorConfig compliance validation fails on GTK script
findings.title: Use mandated two-space indentation in GTK script

findings.description: The newly added shell script indents the first-level body under `if` by four spaces, while root .editorconfig requires indent_size = 2 for all files. An EditorConfig standards check flags the new file; reindent it to two spaces per level.
findings.failureMode: EditorConfig compliance validation fails on GStreamer script
findings.title: Use mandated two-space indentation in GStreamer script

findings.description: When tab swiping is enabled, both leading and trailing constraints now attach to the right skeleton (with positive width), requiring the toolbar's leading edge to be to the right of its trailing edge. Auto Layout breaks constraints/collapses the address toolbar instead of keeping it between left and right skeletons. Restore the left skeleton as the leading anchor.
findings.failureMode: Invalid/unsatisfiable address-toolbar constraints with tab swiping enabled; toolbar may be compressed or misplaced.
findings.title: Anchor the toolbar to the left skeleton again

findings.description: When toolbar actions are reconfigured, new trailing page buttons start at alpha 0; `updateToolbarLayout` iterates the browser actions twice and never includes the trailing page actions, so their icons remain invisible even after animation. Include `trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews` instead of the second browser stack.
findings.failureMode: New trailing page action stays invisible on initial/configuration updates.
findings.title: Restore trailing page actions to the alpha update

findings.description: With a trailing page action (e.g. reload) but no leading action, the new check sets the divider width to 0 even though it separates the location view from the trailing actions; conversely a leading-only action adds a divider before an empty trailing stack. Check the trailing page stack as before the rename.
findings.failureMode: Wrong width/spacing of location divider for configurations where leading and trailing actions differ.
findings.title: Determine divider spacing from the trailing actions

findings.description: On iOS 17+, every iPad onboarding test and the bottom-placement test return from tearDown before app.terminate() and super.tearDown(), leaving the app running and skipping base cleanup. Only skip the theme reset, then always execute teardown.
findings.failureMode: Onboarding test on iPad or bottom placement on iPhone finishes with running application and skips base lifecycle cleanup, contaminating subsequent UI tests.
findings.title: Preserve teardown after skipping theme change

findings.description: On iOS 17+ iPads, testFirstRunTourDarkMode selects Dark via the Appearance screen, yet `|| iPad()` skips its previous Light reset. ThemeManager stores that selection in UserDefaults.standard (not the profile prefs cleared at launch), so subsequent tests start in Dark. Keep the Light reset for tests that set Dark, even if iPad's toolbar-placement option is unavailable.
findings.failureMode: Running the dark-mode onboarding test on iPad leaves a persisted Dark theme in later UI tests.
findings.title: Reset the theme after the iPad dark-mode tour

findings.description: Renaming testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders to verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders removes the test prefix XCTest uses to discover tests; the bookmark Reminders share path no longer runs on any test plan. Restore the test prefix.
findings.failureMode: iOS 17 bookmark->Reminders share regression passes CI untested; existing test no longer discovered.
findings.title: Keep bookmark Reminders assertion discoverable

findings.description: `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` is not an XCTest test method, so the full-functional run (which does not skip ShareLongPressTests) silently stops executing the only bookmark-to-Reminders assertion. Restore the `test` prefix to retain coverage of that share flow.
findings.failureMode: FullFunctionalTestPlan silently ceases running bookmark Reminders verification
findings.title: Keep bookmark Reminders method discoverable by XCTest

findings.description: On iOS 17+, every iPad onboarding test and the bottom-placement test returns here, skipping app.terminate() and super.tearDown(). A skipped iPad test or completed placement test leaves the app running and misses base test cleanup; skip only the theme reset and let the common cleanup run.
findings.failureMode: iOS 17 iPad onboarding run leaves app running and bypasses BaseTestCase teardown, leaking state into following UI tests
findings.title: Do not return before onboarding teardown cleanup

findings.description: testFirstRunTourDarkMode explicitly switches to Dark on iPad too, but `|| iPad()` suppresses its Light reset in tearDown on iOS 17+. After that test the simulator stays in dark appearance, affecting tests that expect default Light. Exempt only tests whose theme really must be preserved, not every iPad test.
findings.failureMode: iOS 17 iPad testFirstRunTourDarkMode leaves saved dark theme enabled for subsequent tests
findings.title: Reset dark theme after iPad dark-mode tour

findings.description: `useAtomGetAllSchedules` returns this newly declared type and `ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper` passes each schedule to `getScheduleListItemData`, which requires `availability[].days: number[]`. Declaring the days as `string[]` makes the mainline schedule list fail TypeScript compilation; the Prisma-backed list handler returns numeric days. Change this field to `number[]`.
findings.failureMode: Schedule list compilation fails because string[] days cannot be passed to transformer requiring number[].
findings.title: Keep availability days numeric for schedule list transformer

findings.description: `useAvailableSlots` now returns this locally declared response, but `EventTypeCalendarViewComponent` passes `schedule.data` into `useAvailableTimeSlots`, whose `IGetAvailableSlots` contract has `fromUser.id: number` (from `IFromUser`). Declaring `id: string` makes `GetAvailableSlotsResponse` non-assignable and fails TypeScript compilation for the calendar view; use `number`. Runtime OOO slots also carry numeric host IDs.
findings.failureMode: TypeScript compile fails when passing atom slot response to useAvailableTimeSlots due to string vs number fromUser.id.
findings.title: Keep OOO host ID numeric to preserve calendar-view typechecking

findings.description: The expanded noRestrictedImports pattern matches two existing atoms imports of `@calcom/trpc/components/QueryCell` in the conferencing-apps and selected-calendars wrappers. Biome lint on either file now errors, blocking lint checks/pre-commit. Replace both imports or adjust restriction to avoid rejecting remaining dependencies.
findings.failureMode: Lint fails on two unchanged atoms components after widening Biome restriction.
findings.title: Migrate existing atoms imports before banning all trpc imports

findings.description: The new validator uses single-quoted literals despite the configured double-quote rule. `biome format packages/platform/atoms/hooks/schedules/types.ts` exits with an error on this condition/error message; change these literals to double quotes.
findings.failureMode: Biome formatting check fails on newly added validation literals.
findings.title: Use Biome's configured quotes for object validation

findings.description: The new name check and error message use single-quoted literals despite the configured double-quote rule. `biome format` reports a formatting error for these lines; use double quotes.
findings.failureMode: Biome formatting check fails on newly added name validation literals.
findings.title: Use Biome's configured quotes for name validation

findings.description: If the executor returns `{'result': None}` or omits `result`, `get` leaves `rendered` as None; the guard permits it and returns it from a method declared `-> str`. `basedpyright` reports `reportReturnType` at this changed return line, so the required type-check fails. Reject None alongside non-string values before returning; this also prevents `len(None)` in the caller (although the old node also crashed for invalid executor outputs).
findings.failureMode: Required strict type check fails with reportReturnType on the newly added renderer.
findings.title: Reject None to satisfy the renderer's string contract

findings.description: Each newly added `_run` test constructs TemplateTransformNode with `graph=mock_graph`, but neither TemplateTransformNode nor its Node base constructor accepts `graph`; the first added test fails with TypeError before executing its assertions, as do the others. Use the supported constructor arguments (and valid `{id, data}` config) so the added tests can run.
findings.failureMode: All newly added tests instantiate an invalid node, failing before checking rendering.
findings.title: Remove unsupported graph argument from newly added tests

findings.description: All 23 added `_run` tests pass bare `node_data` as `config` (starting with this call), but `Node.__init__` requires an `id` inside config and loads variables and template from `config['data']`. After removing the unsupported `graph` kwarg, they still fail with `ValueError('Node ID is required.')`. Pass `{'id': 'test_node', 'data': node_data}` to each new construction.
findings.failureMode: All new tests fail node configuration validation instead of exercising rendering.
findings.title: Pass valid config shape to the new node tests

findings.description: For `SET foo bar` in cluster mode, `keys[1]` is zero-initialized so the extra iteration hashes `argv[0]` (`SET`) and incorrectly replies CROSSSLOT; a key in the same slot as `SET` also writes slot_buffer[1] beyond its one-element allocation. Change `<=` to `<` to avoid wrong replies and heap corruption.
findings.failureMode: Ordinary keyed cluster commands get CROSSSLOT; matching command slots overflow the buffer
findings.title: Do not hash one key past the result

findings.description: With memory pressure, malloc can return NULL and the subsequent slot_buffer[0] dereference crashes the server for any cluster key command; the new allocation also bypasses Redis's required tracked allocator. Use zmalloc with matching zfree (or remove this unnecessary buffer).
findings.failureMode: OOM on a cluster key command dereferences an unchecked malloc result
findings.title: Allocate temporary slots through zmalloc

findings.description: For a cluster command with at least one key, the inclusive loop reads keys[numkeys] and writes slot_buffer[numkeys], outside both arrays; normal SET/GET preprocessing may crash or corrupt memory. Restore an exclusive upper bound.
findings.failureMode: Out-of-bounds access on key slot extraction
findings.title: Do not process a nonexistent extra key

findings.description: `make REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror"` now fails compiling cluster.c: malloc at line 1110 and free at 1120/1124 are marked deprecated in server.h, in addition to bypassing required tracked allocation. Remove the unnecessary buffer or replace its allocation/deallocation with zmalloc/zfree.
findings.failureMode: Required -Werror build fails with deprecated malloc/free calls
findings.title: Replace raw malloc/free so -Werror builds compile

findings.description: MembersAPI is required by `members/api.js`; the implementation still lives at `lib/magic-link/MagicLink.js`. On a case-sensitive filesystem this top-level lowercase require throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND while loading the members service and prevents Ghost startup; restore the PascalCase filename.
findings.failureMode: Members service load fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND before startup.
findings.title: Restore the MagicLink require path

findings.description: `boot.js` calls `emailAnalytics.init()` at startup, but `EmailEventStorage.js` remains unrenamed. This new require resolves to no file on a case-sensitive filesystem, so Ghost startup throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND; require the existing PascalCase filename instead.
findings.failureMode: Ghost startup fails during emailAnalytics.init() due to MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
findings.title: Restore the EmailEventStorage require path

findings.description: `boot.js` invokes email analytics init; `EmailEventProcessor.js` has not been renamed. Once the preceding storage import is repaired, this new require still throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND on a case-sensitive filesystem and prevents startup. Point it at `../email-service/EmailEventProcessor`.
findings.failureMode: Ghost startup fails at EmailEventProcessor import after storage import fixed.
findings.title: Restore the EmailEventProcessor require path

findings.description: Nine rewritten top-level `require` declarations omit the semicolons that were present in base; this violates the required semicolon rule and will fail the server lint step. Retain semicolons on each declaration.
findings.failureMode: Running the server lint check reports missing semicolons in members-api.js.
findings.title: Restore semicolons on rewritten requires

findings.description: After SelectLightTheme, this reads darkThemeView rather than lightThemeView; the dark selection remains 0 so the subsequent XCTAssertEqual(..., "1") fails and prevents the remaining theme transitions from being tested.
findings.failureMode: testCheckSystemThemeChanges fails as soon as it selects Light theme.
findings.title: Read the Light selection from the Light theme button

findings.description: After tapping TopSitesSettings and flipping its switch, the current navigation page is TopSitesSettingsViewController, which doesn't create a Done button. The new `app.buttons["Done"].waitAndTap()` runs on that page before `navigator.goto(NewTabScreen)` can pop it, so testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection times out instead of checking the homepage.
findings.failureMode: Running testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection with Shortcuts page open fails at waitAndTap on nonexistent Done button.
findings.title: Back out of Shortcuts before tapping Done

findings.description: Typing an event followed by a newline (or clearing the textarea) stores an empty string in `trigger.expect`. The server builds a regex from every expected event, so `['prefect.foo','']` produces a pattern with an empty alternative that matches every event; the saved automation fires for unrelated events. Trim/filter blank lines before updating the form.
findings.failureMode: User enters 'prefect.foo\n' and reactive automation fires on any event rather than only prefect.foo.
findings.title: Discard empty event names when parsing the textarea

findings.description: A proactive pool 'Stays in Ready' stores Ready in `expect`, not `after`. The first Ready event is counted as an expected event, so the alert does not fire after the selected 30-second window (it may only fire in a later empty window). Store the proactive selected status in `trigger.after`, as the deployment/flow-run fields do.
findings.failureMode: Pool enters Ready and stays there: proactive 30-second alert does not fire at the end of that 30-second window.
findings.title: Start the proactive work-pool window with `after`

findings.description: For a proactive queue 'Stays in Ready' the select still writes to `trigger.expect`. The first Ready event is counted against threshold 1 rather than opening a window using `after`; after 30 seconds in Ready the alert does not fire (and may instead fire only after a subsequent empty window). Bind the select to `trigger.after` for proactive posture.
findings.failureMode: Queue enters Ready and remains Ready: 30-second proactive alert misses the first 30-second window.
findings.title: Start the proactive work-queue window with `after`

findings.description: Setting strict to false disables strict checking across the entire ui-v2 app, allowing new nullability and implicit-any errors to pass validate:types instead of blocking builds. Keep strict true and fix any new type errors in the components.
findings.failureMode: A new invalid type usage that previously failed validate:types is accepted in CI.
findings.title: Restore strict TypeScript checking

findings.description: The new deployment, custom, work-pool and work-queue proactive `within` inputs allow 5 seconds (custom:78, work-pool:94, work-queue:94). The wizard's `z.number().min(0)` accepts it, but the backend rejects any nonzero duration under 10 seconds; this generates a trigger that cannot be submitted to the server. Add proactive-specific duration validation consistent with the backend.
findings.failureMode: Proactive trigger with within=5 passes UI validation but fails server EventTrigger validation.
findings.title: Validate proactive durations against the server minimum

findings.description: The new work-queue, deployment and custom threshold handlers convert numeric input with `Number` (deployment:82, custom:63), while the wizard only checks `z.number().min(1)`. Pasting `2.5` passes the wizard and yields a trigger whose `threshold` is 2.5 even though the server's event trigger requires an integer, so submission to the server is rejected. Validate integer thresholds in the form.
findings.failureMode: Entering 2.5 in a new queue/deployment/custom threshold passes frontend validation but server rejects the resulting event trigger.
findings.title: Reject fractional thresholds before proceeding

findings.description: Pasting `2.5` into the pool Threshold input calls `parseInt` and replaces the entered value with `2`. The wizard accepts and outputs a different threshold instead of reporting that a non-integer threshold is invalid; parse the full number and enforce integer validation.
findings.failureMode: Pasting 2.5 into the pool threshold emits 2.
findings.title: Do not truncate pasted work-pool thresholds
